tldr: TREE-PLANNER reframes LLM-based close-loop task planning into plan sampling, action tree construction, and grounded deciding phases, reducing token consumption by up to 92.2% while achieving state-of-the-art performance.
contributions: Proposing TREE-PLANNER that decomposes LLM queries into a single plan-sampling call and multiple grounded-deciding calls
Introducing an action tree structure that aggregates sampled plans to enable efficient backtracking during error correction
Demonstrating significant token and correction efficiency improvements on VirtualHome household tasks
methods: TREE-PLANNER operates in three phases: (1) Plan Sampling — an LLM samples N potential plans in a single call using commonsense knowledge; (2) Action Tree Construction — sampled plans are aggregated into a tree where shared prefixes are merged into common branches; (3) Grounded Deciding — the LLM makes top-down decisions at each node based on real-time observations, choosing among child nodes. When an action fails, the method marks invalid subtree nodes and backtracks to the nearest valid fork node rather than replanning from scratch.
results: TREE-PLANNER achieves state-of-the-art results in VirtualHome, surpassing best baselines by 1.29% (with correction) and 3.65% (without correction) in success rate. Token costs are reduced by 53.29% vs ITERATIVE-PLANNER (no correction), 74.36% vs LOCAL REPLAN, and 92.24% vs GLOBAL REPLAN. Error corrections decrease by 37.99% vs LOCAL REPLAN and 40.52% vs GLOBAL REPLAN. Formal analysis derives a critical value of N < 197.72 for token efficiency.
limitations: Requires heuristic setting of sampling number N (set to 25 or 50 in experiments)
Manual error analysis identifies potential areas for improvement
The approach is evaluated only in the VirtualHome simulated environment
Dependence on OpenAI GPT-3.5 API limits generalizability to other LLM backbones
